name: Async Clipboard write
plain: Puts text or images onto the clipboard.
meaning: Can overwrite what the person copied, for example swapping a crypto address. Allowed on a click without a prompt in all browsers.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; needs transient activation or (Chromium) the clipboard-write permission, which is auto-granted to the active tab.

limits.headline: Can put text or images on your clipboard when you tap a button
limits.user_action: You tap Copy link, Copy code or a similar button
can: Copy text, links or images onto your clipboard after a tap or click
Replace whatever you had copied before
Work without any pop up in most browsers
cannot: Copy to your clipboard while you are not using the page, on most browsers
Stop you from pasting something else afterward
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari all allow it after a tap. Samsung Internet support is limited.

story.what_it_is: A site puts text or images on your clipboard, usually when you tap Copy.

marketing.name: Async Clipboard API
marketing.pitch: Google describes it as a modern way for pages to copy text and images with a simple call after a click.

story.for_you: You press a 'Copy link' or 'Copy code' button and a small note says Copied. You can then paste it anywhere. It happens on your tap and usually shows no prompt.
story.for_makers: Copy buttons cut friction for sharing, referral codes, invite links, and code. Makers use them to spread links and track how many people share.

use_cases.example: A browser game has a 'Copy invite link' button so a player can paste it to friends in chat and fill a lobby.
A share sheet button copies a post link in one tap.
A checkout page copies a discount code so a shopper can paste it at the store.
A docs site gives a Copy button on every code block.
A crypto or payment page copies a wallet address, and a bad site could swap in a different one.
A team counts how many people click Copy to measure what content gets shared.

technical_bounds: Needs a gesture in Firefox and Safari
Cannot read after write without permission
